To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

in patients with dysautonomic symptoms, a search for a paraneoplastic cause is mandatory and the diagnosis is based on the association between dysautonomia, the presence of a systemic cancer, and the detection of immunological and/or endocrinological abnormalities.

(1) the onset of systemic cancers is heralded by dysauto-nomia and a neurological non metastatic complication mediated by endocrine and immunological factors; (2) the autonomic neuropathy is a paraneoplastic syndrome; (3) the paraneoplastic limbic encephalo-pathy is associated with autonomic symptoms and signs, which are often the presenting features of the disease; (4) the syndrome of inappropriate ADHI secretion may be associated with LEMS
In summary, our research is concerned with
a series of patients with dysautonomic symptoms, in which the onset of cancer is accompanied by a non-metastasis neurological involvement.
the clinical features, immunological and endocrinologic findings of four patients affected by paraneoplastic syndromes with dysautonomic symptoms.
the clinical and immunological features of paraneoplastic dysautonomias.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
in the patients described here, the autonomic nervous systems was involved in paraneoplasia.

(1) the presence of dysautonomic symptoms in cancer patients is not necessarily related to the direct involvement of the nervous system by metastatic lesions, (2) the dysautonomic syndrome may be a manifestation of an immunological and/or endocrinological disorder, (3) in some patients with cancer the dysautonomic manifestations may be the first sign of a paraneoplastic disorder.
the autonomic nervous involvement in paraneoplasias may have different clinical presentations.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the paraneoplastic dysautonomias are not only a rare but also an important clinical problem, because they may be the initial manifestation of a neoplastic disease and may be associated with non-neurological paraneoplastic complications.
the paraneoplastic involvement of the autonimc nervous system can be mediated by immunological factors and/or endocrine abnormalities.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the autonomic nervous dysfunction may be a presenting symptom in paraneoplasia, and may be a harbinger of a cancer.
the onset of dysautonomic symptoms should prompt a search for a neoplastic disease, and that the presence of dysautonomia and/or neurological symptoms may be the first sign of cancer.
in the presence of a dysautonomic syndrome with neurological involvement, it is necessary to investigate the presence of a systemic cancer.
